title: Original WAByteBuffer binary-string and buffer conversion contracts
oracle: Literal byte/code-unit mappings and independent host arithmetic/seeded byte profiles supply expected bytes and binary strings. All 256 byte values, chunk boundaries, typed-view sentinels, actual returned-buffer identity and shared-empty identities are covered with original exports. Error names distinguish source Error message prefixes from native DataView/access TypeErrors. No vendor output generated the expectations.

trials.configurationScope: one empty supported static gate assignment across the complete six-module conversion/error closure
trials.executionStatus: locally observed: explicit diagnostic process runCase and unchanged baseline/candidate comparisons at both source pins; 28 focused tests pass (27 actual cases plus one portable plan test)

limitations: Only supported gate APIs and static key expressions are inventoried.

exclusions: Binary strings map byte values to UTF-16 code units 0..255; no UTF-8/text codec or protocol encoding compliance is claimed.
Only the four own exported conversion functions execute. Internal ByteBuffer construction, cursor/limit mutation, force-copy flags and prototype/property selectors are not exposed.
Typed view snapshots establish selected bytes only. Strict identity is asserted only for actual source-returned retained ArrayBuffers; no argument-retention or backing-buffer alias proof is inferred.
Lengths, strings, numeric/coercion inputs and histories remain unbounded. Complete supported static gate inventory supplies one empty finite assignment, not exhaustive data or semantic proof.
Loose malformed buffer-decoder branches are source characterization, not supported buffer validation or native-brand/security guarantees.
No provider, Babel helper fixture, host buffer/function/crypto object, storage, network, timers or custom wrapper is supplied.

Locally observed diagnostic process execution is not container proof or production TypeScript scheduling. Original browser bootstrap, named-library parity and full protocol/media acceptance remain unexercised.
